items.identity: Cranach, Melancholy, 1532, KMSsp722
facts: Official collection highlight
Winged central figure sits inactive amid busy children and measuring tools
items.comparison: Other Cranach Melancholy versions exist; importance rests on complex scheme and quality, not uniqueness

items.identity: Cornelis Cornelisz., The Fall of the Titans, 1588-1590, KMS1
facts: Bought by Christian IV in 1621 and recorded in the royal Kunstkammer
items.comparison: Large Northern Mannerist mythological paintings survive elsewhere; scale, quality, and royal provenance combine here

items.identity: Rubens, Christ on the Cross, KMSsp186
facts: Official attribution to Peter Paul Rubens
Displayed in room 204 at API check
items.comparison: Not presented as a unique version; value comes from bodily force and old-master collection context

items.identity: Rembrandt, Study of an Old Man in Profile, c.1628-1632, KMS1636
facts: Small wood-panel head study
SMK technical examination supports early Rembrandt attribution
items.comparison: Many Rembrandt/workshop tronies survive; early date and technical evidence define this example

items.identity: Rembrandt and workshop, Sketch for The Knight with the Falcon, 1659-1661, KMS1384
facts: Related finished painting is in Gothenburg
SMK notes possible workshop participation
items.comparison: A compositional study, not a second complete version of the Gothenburg painting

items.identity: C.W. Eckersberg, Self-Portrait, 1807-1810, KMS1764
facts: Early-career self-portrait
Eckersberg later became a central academy teacher
items.comparison: Not his sole self-portrait or best-known work; useful as the opening of the Golden Age teaching line

items.identity: C.W. Eckersberg, Study of Clouds over the Sea, 1826, KMS6433
facts: Low horizon gives most of the panel to clouds
Part of Eckersberg's observational practice
items.comparison: Cloud studies also central to Constable; this example connects observation to Danish academy practice

items.identity: Christen Kobke, Lake Sortedam from Dosseringen, 1838, KMS359
facts: Official highlight
SMK states it holds 61 of roughly 200 surviving Kobke paintings
items.comparison: World's largest Kobke group makes this representative work part of a unique comparative concentration

items.identity: Christen Kobke, View of Dosseringen towards Norrebro, c.1841-1845, KMS3613
facts: Smaller, tighter view of familiar Copenhagen surroundings
Displayed in room 217D
items.comparison: Value increases through direct comparison with KMS359 rather than treating each view as a separate rare asset

items.identity: Constantin Hansen, A Group of Danish Artists in Rome, 1837, KMS3236
facts: Identifiable Danish expatriate artists
Room details document professional and social identity
items.comparison: Among the clearest group images for explaining the Golden Age artist network in Rome

items.identity: Wilhelm Bendz, The Life Class, 1826, KMS54
facts: Documents Royal Academy teaching
Nude model, students, teacher and casts share one room
items.comparison: European academy scenes exist; local institutional specificity gives this one its value

items.identity: Wilhelm Bendz, A Sculptor in his Studio, 1827, KMS62
facts: Shows live model and intermediate sculptural stages
Studio represented as work site
items.comparison: Pairs with KMS54 to connect training and production

items.identity: Martinus Rorbye, Greeks Working in the Ruins of the Acropolis, 1835, KMS4299
facts: Modern Greek labour appears within ancient ruins
Made during the Acropolis transition into a national archaeological monument
items.comparison: Unlike depopulated classical views, this retains contemporary use and labour

items.identity: Elisabeth Jerichau Baumann, An Egyptian Pot Seller at Gizeh, 1876-1878, KMS8791
facts: Official collection highlight
Artist travelled in the eastern Mediterranean and Egypt
items.comparison: Must hold sitter agency and European Orientalist market expectations together

items.identity: P.S. Kroyer, Boys Bathing at Skagen, 1899, KMS1658
facts: Dusk seascape with moving bathers
Displayed in room 224
items.comparison: One of several Skagen blue-hour works, distinguished by group movement across the shore

items.identity: L.A. Ring, At the French Windows, 1897, KMS3716
facts: Sigrid Ring was pregnant
SMK notes the artist added the dead branch as a memento mori
items.comparison: Not unique as a doorway figure; unusually tight union of biography, threshold geometry and mortality symbolism

items.identity: Edvard Munch, Summer Evening, 1889, KMS2070
facts: Single seated woman on a shoreline
Made during transition toward psychological symbolism
items.comparison: Not a Scream-level icon; useful evidence for landscape becoming psychological structure

items.identity: Vilhelm Hammershoi, Interior in Strandgade, 1901, KMS3696
facts: Artist's home also served as studio and subject
SMK is one of the world's largest Hammershoi collections
items.comparison: Many Strandgade interiors survive; this is an especially complete people-free light-and-space example within the strongest group

items.identity: Vilhelm Hammershoi, Ida with a Teacup, 1907, KMS3352
facts: Ida appears absorbed in a small action
Limited tonal range joins figure and room
items.comparison: Counters the idea that Hammershoi's method depends only on back-turned figures

items.identity: Anna Ancher, A Funeral, 1891, KMS1433
facts: Pale coffin surrounded by black-clad group
Gazes do not converge
items.comparison: Value lies in independent colour and group psychology, not only Skagen School representation

items.identity: Michael Ancher, The Lifeboat is Taken through the Dunes, 1883, KMS1222
facts: Rescue preparation rather than final rescue
Collective bodily effort is the compositional centre
items.comparison: Contrasts with leisure-oriented Skagen beach scenes

items.identity: Henri Matisse, Portrait of Madame Matisse. The Green Line, 1905, KMSr171
facts: SMK names it among its ten greatest highlights
Central green stripe structures warm and cool halves
items.comparison: Not the only Fauvist masterpiece; a pivotal 1905 portrait and core of SMK's 25-work Matisse group

items.identity: Henri Matisse, Goldfish, 1912, KMSr82
facts: Orange fish anchor the palette
Fishbowl combines elevated and frontal viewpoints
items.comparison: One of several Matisse goldfish paintings; comparative group in SMK matters

items.identity: Henri Matisse, Self-Portrait, 1906, KMSr78
facts: Striped shirt and non-natural colour
Made directly after the 1905 Fauvist controversy
items.comparison: Not unique; proximity to Green Line shows the method applied to the artist himself

items.identity: Andre Derain, Woman in a Chemise, 1906, KMSr14
facts: Official French-modernism highlight
Hard contours and red-green contrast structure the body
items.comparison: Direct comparison with Matisse distinguishes two Fauvist approaches

items.identity: Pablo Picasso, Houses in Gosol, c.1906, KMSr92
facts: Linked to Picasso's Gosol stay
Buildings compressed into ochre blocks
items.comparison: Not the first Cubist painting; preserves the transition before full Cubism

items.identity: Georges Braque, Trees at l'Estaque, 1908, KMSr7
facts: Part of the early Cubist l'Estaque context
Restricted earth palette and compressed depth
items.comparison: Related l'Estaque works survive in multiple museums; this is one of the limited transition examples

items.identity: Asger Jorn, The Sun is Pissing Me Off, 1961, KMS8657
facts: Title contributes an explicit emotional register
Surface retains scraping, dripping and overpainting
items.comparison: Louisiana has a larger Jorn concentration; SMK work anchors the national modern line

items.identity: Sonja Ferlov Mancoba, Mask and Figure, 1977-1984, KMS8889
facts: Openings make background part of the sculpture
Long working period is reflected in layered form
items.comparison: Best understood within SMK's group rather than as a lone exotic-looking object

items.identity: Bjorn Norgaard, Objects from The Horse Sacrifice, 1970, KMS8603
facts: Remains and documentation derive from a real horse sacrifice action
Now preserved by the national museum
items.comparison: Not the only animal-based performance in modern art; unique value is the specific Danish event and preservation chain
